title: One More Makes the Next Number

steps.body: Add one more toy and the count does not start over — it simply says the NEXT number. One more than five is six, always.
steps.narration: Add one more toy and the count does not start over — it simply says the NEXT number. One more than five is six, always.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 13? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 13 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 14.
15 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 13 lands on 14.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 13 and count on 1: you land on 14.
widget.successFeedback: 14 — one hop forward, because each number is exactly one more than the last.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 14.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 13 means one hop, stopping on 14.

predict.prompt: A group of 5 gets one more toy. The new count is…
predict.reveal: One more moves the count forward by exactly one word: from five to six.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch one larger.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch one larger.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

options.feedback: Correct — each counting number is exactly one more than the number before it.
14 is the number we started from, not the one that follows it.
16 skips a number; counting moves one at a time.
13 comes BEFORE 14; the count moves forward, not back.
